Q: Can a transactional consistency boundary in DDD change depending on the method? A:

No, the transaction boundary shouldn't change depending on the context. Transaction boundaries should never intersect or else it wouldn't be clear anymore who is responsible for keeping a specific part of the domain model consistent (and with which other parts of the model). Or in other words: Aggregates are meant to partition the domain model into mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive transaction boundaries, so it is always clear what is kept consistent by database transactions and what you need to keep consistent by application logic (e.g. domain events).

For your specific problem, a solution could look like this:

  • Questions and Groups are independent aggregate types

  • A Question can optionally reference a group (by name?)

  • When you create a Question that references a group for the first time, a new Group aggregate is created by a domain event and the Question is added to it (by ID reference)

  • If you reference an existing Group in a new Question, the question is added (by ID reference) to the group by a domain event

Honestly, I'm not sure what you mean with your business rules 2 and 3, can you be more specific?

Q: List of Javascript mobile events A:

Most modern mobile browsers (Chrome, Safari, Edge) are moving toward Pointer Events. These are designed to handle mouse, touch, and stylus input with a single API. If you aren't using these, you're likely working harder than you need to.

  • pointerdown / pointerup / pointermove

  • pointerover / pointerout

  • pointerenter / pointerleave

  • pointercancel: Extremely important for mobile (triggered when the system takes over, like an incoming call).

Q: Print out plot with unicode symbol to PDF A:

Your code works for me using R version 4.5.1 ggplot2_4.0.0 and Windows 10.

You can force a font that supports utf8 like Arial Unicode MS

library(showtext)
library(ggplot2)

download.file("https://github.com/stamen/toner-carto/raw/master/fonts/Arial-Unicode-Regular.ttf", destfile = "Arial-Unicode-Regular.ttf", mode = "wb")
font_add(family = "Arial", regular = "Arial-Unicode-Regular.ttf")
showtext_auto()
pdf("plot2.pdf", width=11, height=8)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + 
   geom_point(shape=sprintf('\u2605'), size=5) + 
   theme(text = element_text(family = "Arial"))
dev.off()

giving

Or you can try

  • using geom_text
  • ggsave with type="cairo" or with device = "cairo_pdf"
  • loading emojifont-namespace

Q: Abbreviations/Acronyms for Quarto A:

There is now a Quarto extension called acronyms. You can install it in your Quarto project via this command:

quarto add rchaput/acronyms

This package is an extension of Quarto, which supports, among others, MS Word / HTML outputs.

How to use

After installing the extension, you need to add is as a filter to _quarto.yml project configuration:

project:
    website
filters:
    - acronyms

Then, in your .md or .qmd document, add the acronyms list to the yml configuration preamble:


---
acronyms:
    keys:
        - shortname: HTML
        - longname: HyperText Markup Language
---

Then you can use it in your document either like:

This is some \acr{HTML} element

or with Quarto shortcodes:

This is some {{< acr HTML >}} element

Link to docs if you want to learn more.

Q: How do I implement a cylindrical grid for a 3D plot? A:

You should care about legibility and reader psychofidelity first, and what you consider to be attractive about fourth. Psychofidelity is only harmed and not helped by insisting on a three-dimensional projection. You would do better to produce a 2D plot with a colourized curve using something like the Viridis scale. This will avoid foreshortening, etc.
